passage:
Pranav had ended it on Friday, gently, on a call. By Monday Ishita had checked his profile maybe fifty times. Board prelims started Wednesday. And the worst part: they were in the same physics tuition, four seats apart.
Her chest felt hollow, as if someone had scooped it out. At tuition she kept her eyes on the whiteboard and still knew exactly where he was sitting.
That night she opened a new story and typed, "Some people only care till someone better comes along." Her thumb hovered.
Her cousin Meenal, on the other bed, saw the screen. "Delete that. Please. Tomorrow you'll hate it." Then she took Ishita's phone, put it in the cupboard, and made two mugs of cocoa. "You can cry and study at the same time, you know. I did it for my twelfth."
Ishita laughed and cried at once. It still hurt. But for an hour, it hurt a little less.

qa.q: When did Board prelims start?
qa.a: Board prelims started Wednesday.

qa.q: What does Ishita checking Pranav's profile fifty times suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Ishita feels rejected and can't let go yet; the hollow feeling pulls her back to him again and again.

qa.q: How did Meenal help Ishita in a wise way?
qa.a: Meenal stopped a hurtful post, put the phone away and stayed with Ishita, showing that the pain is real and that she can still get through exams. 🤍

qa.q: What might Pranav feel sitting four seats away in tuition?
qa.a: Pranav may feel awkward and a little guilty, knowing Ishita is hurting even though he ended it gently.

grounding: Shows a teen left after a breakup feeling hollow and checking his profile, leaning on a cousin and holding back a retaliatory post.

subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
Three days after Rudra ended it, Minakshi was still in her school uniform at seven in the evening, lying on the bed in their Salt Lake flat, scrolling. His new profile picture. A comment from a girl in his class. Scroll, refresh, scroll.
Her older sister Bhavna came in without knocking, sat on the edge of the bed and held out her hand. "Phone. Just for an hour."
"I'm not doing anything."
"You're doing the thing I did at your age. Give."
Minakshi handed it over and then, without warning, started crying. "It feels like there's a hole right here," she said, pressing her chest.
"I know," Bhavna said. "It's real. It's not silly. And it gets smaller. Not tomorrow. But it does."
Later Ma brought luchi, and the three of them ate on the bed like when Minakshi was little. Nobody mentioned Rudra. Minakshi felt a tiny bit less empty.

qa.q: Where was Minakshi lying three days after the breakup?
qa.a: Minakshi was lying on the bed in their Salt Lake flat, still in her school uniform.

qa.q: What does Minakshi's endless scrolling suggest about how she feels?
qa.a: It suggests Minakshi feels rejected and empty and keeps looking for clues about Rudra's life, which keeps the hurt fresh.

qa.q: What did Bhavna do that helped?
qa.a: Bhavna took the phone for a while, said the pain is real and will get smaller, and stayed close instead of lecturing.

qa.q: How might Bhavna feel watching her sister like this?
qa.a: Bhavna probably feels protective and sympathetic, since she remembers doing the same thing at Minakshi's age.

grounding: Illustrates a teen's grief after being left, with a hollow chest and constant scrolling, eased by leaning on her sister and mother.

subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
Leela had ended it on Sunday, kindly, by the temple tank. By Wednesday, Tanvir still felt as if someone had scooped out his chest.

He checked her profile forty times a day. Her new photo from the Dussehra mela, smiling with her cousins. Every smile felt aimed at him.

On Wednesday night he typed a post about "people who pretend to care." His thumb hovered over Share.

His older brother, Faiz, came onto the roof where Tanvir was sitting. He saw the phone and didn't grab it. He just sat down.

"You want to post that?"

"She's acting like nothing happened."

"Maybe. Or maybe she's sad too and hiding it. Either way, that post will follow you around this whole small town."

Tanvir deleted it. Then, without meaning to, he started crying. Faiz stayed. Later he said, "It's this bad because it mattered. It won't stay this bad."

qa.q: Where did Leela end the relationship?
qa.a: By the temple tank.

qa.q: How does Tanvir feel by Wednesday?
qa.a: He feels hollow and rejected, as if someone had scooped out his chest, and keeps checking Leela's profile.

qa.q: What did Faiz do that helped?
qa.a: He sat with Tanvir without grabbing the phone, talked him out of an angry post, stayed while he cried, and reminded him the pain would ease.

qa.q: Why might Leela seem happy in her photos?
qa.a: She may be sad too and hiding it, as Faiz suggests, or simply trying to move on with her cousins.

grounding: Tanvir feels rejection and a hollow chest after the breakup and nearly posts in anger, but leans on his brother, who reminds him the pain is real and will ease.

subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
Three days after Mats broke up with her, Ulla was still checking his photos in her Stockholm bedroom. He had gone skating with his friends on Saturday, as if nothing had happened. Her chest felt hollow, like a room with the furniture taken out.

She drafted a post, a song lyric about liars. She wanted him to see it.

Xin, her best friend, turned up with cinnamon buns and a blanket. She read the draft over Ulla's shoulder.

"You can post it," Xin said. "But in a week you'll be embarrassed, and he'll show it to everyone."

Ulla closed the app. Then she cried into the blanket for ten minutes, and Xin didn't say anything, just passed tissues.

Later Ulla told her mother everything over dinner. Her mother said, "It hurts this much because you cared. It will get smaller. Not today, but it will."

qa.q: What did Xin bring when she came over?
qa.a: Cinnamon buns and a blanket.

qa.q: What was Ulla feeling when she drafted the post?
qa.a: She felt hurt and angry, wanting Mats to see how much he had hurt her, with a hollow feeling in her chest.

qa.q: Which choices helped Ulla through that evening?
qa.a: Not posting the angry lyric, letting herself cry with Xin, and talking to her mother, who reminded her the pain would ease.

qa.q: How does Xin see the draft post?
qa.a: Xin sees it as something Ulla would regret and that Mats could use against her, so she gently discourages it.

grounding: Ulla, left by Mats, feels a hollow chest and wants to post an angry lyric, but leans on her friend and mother and hears that the pain will ease.

The school counsellor's room smelled of the jasmine the gardener had left on the windowsill. Urmila sat on the plastic chair, sleeves pulled over her hands.

"He broke up with me on Monday," she said. "Sachin. He was nice about it. That's what makes it worse."

"How have you been since?"

"I check his page every hour. I haven't eaten lunch. My chest feels empty, like there's a hole in it."

The counsellor listened, then asked, "Who have you told?"

"My friend Hina. Not my mother."

"Would you be willing to tell your mother tonight? Not the details. Just that you're sad."

Urmila nodded slowly.

"And the checking?"

"I wrote a mean post yesterday. I didn't send it."

"Good. That pain is real, Urmila. And it does ease. Let's meet again on Friday."

qa.q: When did Sachin break up with Urmila?
qa.a: On Monday.

qa.q: What does Urmila mean when she says her chest feels empty?
qa.a: She feels hollow and rejected, grieving the relationship even though Sachin was kind about it.

qa.q: How does the counsellor support Urmila?
qa.a: The counsellor listens, encourages her to tell her mother that evening, affirms not posting the mean message, reminds her the pain eases, and sets a follow-up for Friday.

qa.q: How does the counsellor seem to view Urmila's unsent post?
qa.a: The counsellor sees it as a real strength, saying "Good", because not posting protects Urmila from regret while the pain eases.

grounding: In the school counsellor's room, Urmila, left by Sachin, describes rejection and a hollow chest, and is encouraged to lean on family and avoid retaliatory posts.

subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
Dear Sudha Didi,
You said to write when it felt too big for the phone, so here it is. Manav ended things on Friday. He was kind about it, which somehow makes it worse.
Since then my chest feels hollow, like someone scooped it out. I keep opening his profile to see if he's posted, if he looks happy, who liked what. Forty times yesterday, maybe.
Last night I typed a caption about "people who pretend to care" and my thumb was on Post. Then I remembered you saying, "Don't write anything at midnight that you'd hate at noon," and I deleted it.
Today Meenal came over with samosas and we watched a silly film, and for two whole hours I forgot. Amma hugged me without asking anything.
Tell me honestly: does it really get smaller?
Your Aparna

qa.q: When did Manav end things?
qa.a: Manav ended things on Friday.

qa.q: What is Aparna feeling since Friday, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Aparna feels hurt and hollow, describing a scooped-out chest and checking Manav's profile about forty times in one day.

qa.q: What helped Aparna at this stage, and what could keep helping?
qa.a: Deleting the midnight caption and spending time with Meenal and Amma helped; leaning on people like that, and checking the profile less, lets the pain ease.

qa.q: How might Sudha feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Sudha may feel moved, and glad that the midnight advice stopped the post, and will likely want to reassure Aparna that the pain does get smaller 🤍

grounding: Shows a teenager who was left feeling rejected and hollow, resisting a spiteful post and leaning on friends and family.
